findings.title: Do not claim stopped-child handle retention publishes its completion to owner recovery
findings.evidence: The new design says that if a supported original is retained, stopping leaves its original barrier available to existing owner recovery; plan says the original is retained for existing owner recovery. However malformed-success handling runs before :group_bind. A newly started owner probe record has completion:nil; bind_probe is the operation that stores the completion there. The DOWN handler passes only that held owner record to recover, which reads held.completion and never the dead child final state. For the newly required valid-original+nonnil-upload or wrong-arity successful return, retaining original_request in returned stopped state does not publish it to either owner. The group nil-completion branch marks lifecycle failed and retains the hold; it does not gain access to that child-state handle. This is an incorrect recovery-availability statement, although the mandated stop/no-refund behavior itself is fail closed.
findings.required_change: Make a narrow wording correction in both documents: preserving a supported original in the dropped/stopped child state preserves the transformation identity but is not owner-record publication or proof of cleanup. Existing owner recovery can use only an already bound/stored completion; for pre-bind malformed success the owner may still have completion:nil, and its current fail-closed lifecycle/hold behavior remains authoritative. Keep stop/no-refund and the finite discriminator unchanged. Do not add early binds, death-state inspection, a recovery protocol or a new transport/group completion-publication step to work around this wording in this slice. Any later need to recover these pre-bind originals remains separately designed accounting/activation work.
findings.verification_expected: Revised versioned design/plan must accurately distinguish child-local original retention, prior owner binding and nil-completion hold. Source review of existing bind/DOWN/recover paths suffices for the design correction; no new runtime/test gate is requested by this finding.
